historicalEras.name: Early & Middle Bronze Age
keyDevelopments: Byblos established as Egypt's chief cedar timber and resin supplier
Construction of Byblos L-Shaped Temple (c. 2600 BCE)
Construction of Temple of the Obelisks (c. 1900 BCE)

historicalEras.name: Iron Age Phoenician Golden Age & Colonization
keyDevelopments: Hiram I of Tyre develops island city and Melqart precinct
Royal inscription of King Ahiram at Byblos establishes 22-letter linear alphabet (c. 1000 BCE)
Foundation of Carthage by Tyrian settlers (c. 814 BCE)
West Mediterranean trading stations established at Motya, Gadir (Cádiz), and Tharros

historicalEras.name: Persian Rule & Western Punic Hegemony
keyDevelopments: Sidon becomes flagship fleet commander for Achaemenid Empire
Temple of Eshmun expanded with grand podium by King Bodashtart
Siege of Motya by Dionysius I of Syracuse (397 BCE); engineering of siege towers and catamarans
Phoenician fleet participates in Battle of Salamis (480 BCE)

historicalEras.name: Alexander's Conquest & The Punic Wars
keyDevelopments: Alexander's 7-month siege of Tyre (332 BCE); construction of the 60m mole permanently creating the tombolo peninsula
Punic naval supremacy contested in First Punic War; Battle of the Aegates (241 BCE) and Marsala warship loss
Engineering of the circular military Cothon at Carthage for 220 warships (c. 220 BCE)

exhibitEvents.title: The Geoarchaeological Siege of Tyre (332 BCE)
exhibitEvents.focus: Civil engineering, causeway construction, and coastal sedimentation dynamics
exhibitEvents.pedagogicalApproach: Non-violent architectural logistics and physical geography demonstration

exhibitEvents.title: The Siege of Island Motya (397 BCE)
exhibitEvents.focus: Lagoon geography, causeway assault, and four-story defensive wheeled siege towers
exhibitEvents.pedagogicalApproach: Problem-solving analysis of island fortifications and shallow-water logistics

exhibitEvents.title: Naval Architecture of the Aegates Islands (241 BCE)
exhibitEvents.focus: Forensic archaeology of bronze warship rams and prefabricated hull construction from the Marsala wreck
exhibitEvents.pedagogicalApproach: Nautical archaeology puzzle examining hull timbers and bilingual markings
